three.js -- vendored, pinned copy
==================================

Package:     three
Version:     0.160.0 (r160)
Source:      https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.min.js
Vendored:    2026-08-18
File:        three.min.js (669,884 bytes, self-contained UMD build)

Why r160 specifically, not the latest release
-----------------------------------------------
three.js dropped its global/UMD `build/three.min.js` build starting with
r161 -- from r161 onward the library ships as ES modules only. This
website (website/index.html) is designed to be opened directly via
file:// with no server ("Just open index.html in a browser -- no server
required", see ../README.md). Chrome (and other browsers) always treat
file:// as a cross-origin/opaque origin for `<script type="module">` and
its imports, so an ES-module-only three.js build would fail to load with
a CORS error every time the site is opened this way -- confirmed live
against this exact file during implementation.

r160 is the last release with a working global/UMD build, loaded here as
a plain classic `<script src="vendor/three.min.js" defer>` -- the same
loading pattern already used for app.js -- so `window.THREE` is available
to hero3d.js with no server, no bundler, and no CORS failure.

Do not upgrade this file to a newer three.js release without first
re-solving the file:// / ES-module problem above (e.g. switching the
site's run model to require a local server), or the "open index.html
directly" run mode documented in website/README.md will silently break.

The vendored file itself carries one harmless `console.warn` (not an
error) noting that the global/UMD build is deprecated upstream -- an
accepted, documented trade-off for this project's zero-server requirement.
